newsitem.title: USA: U.S. PC shipments seen rising 13 percent in 1997.
newsitem.headline: U.S. PC shipments seen rising 13 percent in 1997.

text.p: Market Research firm International Data Corp. said Wednesday in its initial forecast for 1997 that it expected the U.S. personal computer industry to ship 13 percent more units next year than in 1996.

IDC also said in a PC Market Outlook conference here that it now projected U.S. PC shipments for the current year will grow to 26.8 million units, up 16.6 percent over 1995 and slightly below the 16.9 percent rate it had earlier predicted.
Eric Lewis, manager of personal systems research at IDC, said Intel Corp.'s upbeat forecast this week for its third quarter revenues, supported IDC's projections.
"To me, it's confirmed we've been right all along, saying its a pretty good year," Lewis said. "Last year was a boom year. This isn't a boom year," he added.
